what: Targets considered, and what became of them. This is MEMORY, not a gate: nothing here refuses anything. It exists because five separate targets died in one session on 2026-08-31, each after hours of work, and every one of them would have died in minutes if the prior art had been read first — and because that intelligence otherwise lives only in commit messages and is lost by the next session.
howToUse: Before committing time to a target, look for it here. If it is listed DEAD, read why and do not re-derive it. If it is not listed, scout it and add a row — including when the answer is OPEN, because a scouted-and-open target is worth more than an unscouted one.

verdicts.OPEN: scouted, nobody owns it, worth work
verdicts.OCCUPIED: someone has done it; beating them is a race, not a gap
verdicts.UNSCOUTED: named but never checked — treat every claim about it as unverified

targets.name: Polynomial multiplication over F2, FULL product P_n
targets.killedBy: Chen & Kauers, arXiv:2502.06264 (Feb 2025) — adapted the Kauers-Moosbauer flip-graph software to polynomial multiplication and published a 10x10 table over Z2. Their squares land exactly ON the Montgomery/CRT bounds: P2=3, P3=6, P4=9, P5=13, P6=17, P7=22, P8=26.
targets.note: Their table is a good CALIBRATION LADDER for any flip-graph walk. Use it that way; do not attack the family.
targets.cost: ~4 hours before the paper was found

targets.name: Polynomial multiplication over F2, TRUNCATED and CYCLIC products
targets.finding: Chen & Kauers do NOT touch these — the words cyclic/truncated/negacyclic do not appear in their paper. But Wang (arXiv:2603.07280) improved T9 from 27 to 26 himself, by flip-graph search over F2, in a FOOTNOTE. So modern search has touched exactly one case, and it won.
targets.measured: Our free walk reproduced published upper bounds exactly at C7 (13, which is optimal), T6 (14) and T7 (18), then landed 1 above at T8 (23 vs 22) and T9 (27 vs 26) and 3 above at C8 (25 vs 22). Laptop-bound, not algorithm-bound.
targets.note: Over F2 the negacyclic product IS the cyclic one (X^n+1 = X^n-1 in characteristic 2). The untested lever is a better SEED: fold a full-product scheme down to the cyclic target, same rank, free, instead of starting at naive rank n^2.

targets.name: Additive complexity of rank-23 3x3 matrix multiplication
targets.killedBy: The record moved SEVEN times in under a year: 98 (Laderman 1976), 62, 61, 60 (arXiv:2508.03857), 59 (arXiv:2601.05272), 58 (arXiv:2512.21980), 56 (arXiv:2604.27645), 55 (arXiv:2607.28676, Jul 2026). Three of those in 2026.
targets.note: Also a representation mismatch: our generation front is F2-only and these are integer schemes over {-1,0,1}. As an AUDIT target it was excellent — the 55 verified here and held. instruments/slp is the reusable part.
targets.cost: the search was abandoned at the gate; the audit took ~1 hour and produced a page

targets.name: Chowla's cosine problem — constructing sets with small c
targets.killedBy: TWO independent reasons. (1) sin-mfg's own chowla-cosine probe carries a literature gate dated 2026-08-20, confidence 9/10, ruling explicit small-c sets OCCUPIED by Mercer (INTEGERS 19 (2019) #A4) and Bedert (arXiv:2509.05260); that lab had already reached c <= 0.6460 at n=20 while our run reached only 0.778. (2) Chowla CONJECTURED K(n) ~ sqrt(n), i.e. c bounded below — so the FrontierMath ask is to refute Chowla's conjecture, and Epoch's own page says 'there is also a risk that Chowla's conjecture is true, in which case the problem is not solvable'.
targets.measured: Our certified c rises with n: 0.6558 (n=10), 0.7073 (15), 0.7781 (20), 0.7733 (25), 0.8205 (30) — parked near the folklore constant 1/sqrt(2), a factor ~15 from the 1/20 landmark, trending the wrong way. Data consistent with the conjecture.
targets.note: THE LESSON: the killing gate was already on disk in sin-mfg. Read that lab BEFORE building, not after. The one live sub-lane is the VERIFIER, not the mathematics — Epoch's sampling check can be fooled (demonstrated: A = 40320*{1..24}, max(A) under their 1e6 ceiling, true c = 1.189981, a 1000-point grid reports 0.2041).
targets.cost: ~3 hours, and the answer was local the whole time

targets.name: Prove delta(f_d) >= 1/2 for large even d
targets.killedBy: delta(f_d) approaches 1 - e^(-1/2) = 0.3934693..., and the density pinned at d = 62 is 0.393469340287. A floor at 1/2 is contradicted by data this project computed itself.
targets.note: Proposed out loud by this project before being checked against its own records. Any proposed bound on delta must be compared against the 283 pinned densities in certs/erdos290-tail-ext.json first.

targets.name: Close a residue class of degrees rather than bounding all of them
targets.measured: A class of density 1/m removes almost exactly 1/m of the bracket width: 49.8% for one degree in two, 33.2% for one in three, 24.9% for one in four. It buys a digit only when the class is nearly everything.
targets.note: Ranked as a promising middle path before it was measured. It is linear where the problem needs exponential.

targets.name: Bound delta(f_d) to a window around 1 - e^(-1/2) for all large even d
targets.scouted: 2026-08-31 (van Doorn read in full, not from the abstract)
targets.why: The #290 bracket width IS the unpinned tail (weight 8.045047e-4, charged delta in [0,1]). Scouted arithmetic replaces the guessed window: the fourth unconditional digit of 1/(1+c) needs delta in (0.0990, 0.5156] for all large even d, NOT the [0.293, 0.493] recorded before — wider than believed on the low side, TIGHTER on the high side. Both ends of that band sit within about 3% of the free bounds below, so a lemma that only just clears them buys nothing robust; a window of width 0.1 centred near 1-e^(-1/2) = 0.3934693 clears both comfortably. Brute force still needs the horizon near 3100 instead of 620.
targets.structure: delta = 1 - E[2^(-fix(sigma))] over pi(G) <= S_l. CORRECTION to the earlier framing: that identity ALREADY presupposes the sign-kernel K = G ∩ C_2^l is large (K = C_2^l gives it exactly; K = even-weight perturbs it by 1/(2^l l!), which is the known delta = delta_hyp(l) - 1/(2^l l!) at d = 8, 24, 48). GIVEN K contains the even-weight module, the size of the image pi(G) is IRRELEVANT to the upper bound: 2^(-t) is convex so Jensen gives E[2^(-fix)] >= 2^(-E[fix]), and Burnside gives E[fix] = 1 for ANY transitive pi(G), hence delta <= 1/2 — no primitivity, no Jordan, no group identification. So the target is NOT how big the image is; it is HOW BIG THE KERNEL IS. K is an S_l-submodule of F_2^l with only four values (0, diag, even, full), but that classification itself needs pi(G) large, and that is where the circularity sits. K in {0, diag} is the dangerous case: there delta can rise toward 1 - 1/e = 0.632, past the 0.5156 ceiling. Lower side: delta >= 1/r for G transitive of rank r on the 2l roots (Diaconis-Fulman-Guralnick, arXiv:0708.2643 — it is Cauchy-Schwarz on E[fix] = 1, E[fix^2] = r), so delta >= 0.0990 follows from rank <= 10 alone. Cameron-Cohen runs the other way (derangements >= (r-1)/n) and is useless here, giving only delta <= 1 - 1/l.
targets.unscouted: RESOLVED. The answer is that NOTHING is known unconditionally. (1) IRREDUCIBILITY IS NOT A THEOREM. van Doorn proves none of it; his proof of Lemma 32 reads: using polisirreducible and GaloisGroup from PARI/GP and Magma, we have found that fd is irreducible for all even d <= 500, while Gd is isomorphic to Sl+ for all even d <= 60, except for d = 8, 24, 48. That is computation to 500, not a proof for large d — and his Lemma 38 (delta = non-derangement proportion) is stated under the irreducibility hypothesis. (2) NO LITERATURE ON Gal(f_d) EXISTS. f_d appears to be studied nowhere but that paper; searches over Galois groups of derivatives of falling factorials, of x(x-1)...(x-d), and of Stirling-coefficient polynomials return nothing on this family. (3) The nearest published analogue is PROBABILISTIC and about a different family: random reciprocal polynomials of large degree have Galois group C_2 wr S_m or one of two index-2 subgroups (arXiv:2510.18857) — the same five-candidate shape, no purchase on a fixed d. (4) The applicable fixed-point literature is Diaconis-Fulman-Guralnick and Cameron-Cohen; both are rank-based, and neither bounds delta from above without kernel information.
targets.worth: REPRICED, and the earlier claim was overstated. Theorem 8 reads 0.54 < liminf (b(a)-a)/log a < 0.61, with Lemma 32 supplying 0.82 < c < 0.85 and the two constants being 1/(1+c) and 1/(2c) rounded to TWO decimals. The THIRD digit (0.54 -> 0.546) is therefore a real sharpening of a published theorem statement — and it is already banked. The FOURTH digit sharpens the OEIS decimal expansion and nothing else, because no theorem anywhere states this constant to four places. Pursue it for the sequence, not for the theorem; the theorem-level win is spent.
targets.openAngle: Untried and cheap to think about: f_d(0) = (-1)^d d!, leading coefficient d+1, h(0) = (-1)^l (l!)^2. A Dumas / Newton-polygon argument at primes dividing d! is exactly the machinery Filaseta and Trifonov used to settle Bessel and generalized Laguerre irreducibility. Nobody has pointed it at f_d. That is the irreducibility half only; the kernel half has no known route.

targets.name: disc(f_d) is a perfect square exactly at d = 4k(k+1)
targets.verdict: OPEN — corollary unclaimed, but the ingredient is not ours
targets.note: Honest split: the disc(f_d) = (d+1)(2^l l! disc h)^2 law is a specialisation of Cullinan, and only the 4k(k+1) characterisation of the exceptional set has no prior art. Re-cite before any submission — AACST2020 does not support the sentence it is attached to, and Cullinan belongs there instead.
targets.finding: The COROLLARY is unclaimed: van Doorn never mentions a discriminant or a square anywhere in arXiv:2411.03073 (full text grepped), and no other paper studies f_d, so nothing in the literature characterises the exceptional degrees as 4k(k+1). THE INGREDIENT IS ANOTHER MATTER, and the preprint gets it wrong twice. It credits the composition-discriminant step to Altmann-Awtrey-Cryan-Shannon-Touchette 2020 and claims the novelty is the NON-MONIC leading factor d+1. But AACST2020 is specifically about x^8 + a x^4 + b (doubly even octics) and contains no general composition law; and the general non-monic law is already written down — John Cullinan, The discriminant of a composition (Bard College note): disc(f o g) = (-1)^e l(f)^(delta-1) l(g)^(...) (disc f)^delta Res(f o g, g prime), with l the leading coefficient, explicitly non-monic. Its hypotheses hold here: disc h and disc(x^2) nonzero, and Res(h, x^2) = h(0)^2 = (l!)^4 nonzero.

targets.name: Does a model proposer beat the free flip walk?
targets.note: SPEC-GENERATION.md says a paid proposer must beat the free baseline before it earns its invoice. The baseline is now nailed down: flip@v1 reaches Laderman's 23 on <3,3,3> over F2 at $0.0000. The paid side has never been run. Cheap, and it settles whether models add anything to this machine.

targets.name: van Doorn Theorem 8's OTHER constant, 0.61, is already improvable at zero cost
targets.verdict: SENT 2026-08-31 — stated publicly, no longer unclaimed
targets.finding: Theorem 8 is TWO-SIDED: 0.54 < liminf (b(a)-a)/log a < 0.61, from Lemma 30 (liminf <= 1/(2c)) and Lemma 31 (liminf >= 1/(1+c)), with Lemma 32's 0.82 < c < 0.85. The upper constant 0.61 = 1/(2 * 0.82) needs a LOWER bound on c — and a lower bound on c needs no tail lemma at all, since the unpinned tail is simply charged 0. Our certified c >= 0.830416407911 gives liminf < 0.6021076 immediately.
targets.why: Everything published from this project — the report page, both issue-164 comments, the OEIS packs — speaks only about 1/(1+c) and the lower constant. The upper constant improves 0.61 -> 0.6022 from the SAME certified data: no window, no new degree, no assumption beyond the Lemma 32 dependency already carried. Theorem 8 would read 0.546 < liminf < 0.6022, narrowing the published interval from width 0.07 to 0.0562.
targets.note: Lemma 30 was read at the source before it was stated (it is an upper bound on the liminf with c the EXACT constant, so a certified lower bound on c plugs straight in). Then published in the issue-164 follow-up, comment 5484039660: liminf <= 1/(2c) <= 0.602107563430 against the published 0.61, with the honest note that the cited horizon already gave 0.603053548709 — almost all of the gain is that 0.82 was a conservative reading of c, and our 250 degrees move it by about 0.001.

targets.name: A benchmark that cannot be contaminated, because instances are minted from a seed
targets.verdict: OPEN — the gap is real, but the prototype currently has ZERO signal
targets.occupied: THE HEADLINE IDEA IS TABLE STAKES, not a differentiator, and anyone in eval will say so in one sentence. Procedural generation to defeat contamination is a crowded, settled field: DyVal (ICLR 2024, DAG-generated instances with controllable complexity), GSM-Symbolic (symbolic templates), LiveBench (monthly refresh plus procedurally generated versions of already-leaked tasks), AntiLeak-Bench, DyCodeEval, and above all REASONING GYM (arXiv:2505.24760, NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight): 100+ procedural generators and verifiers across algebra, arithmetic, logic, graphs and games, explicitly advertising virtually infinite instances with adjustable complexity. Time-gated variants (LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench) cover the same need sociologically. Never pitch 'minted from a seed, therefore uncontaminated' as the novelty — it was novel in 2023.
targets.gap: What is NOT occupied is the conjunction of three properties, and our matmul rung has all three. (1) THE GENERATOR DOES NOT KNOW THE ANSWER. Reasoning Gym and every dynamic benchmark generate a problem together with its answer key, so the task is closed-form recall-checking; ours commissions an open-ended SEARCH (find a rank-R decomposition) and the certifier decides a submission it never anticipated. (2) GRADING IS A DECISION PROCEDURE, not a match or a judge — exact rational arithmetic, so a rejection is proved rather than scored. Proof-graded benchmarks do exist (CLEVER arXiv:2505.13938, VERINA arXiv:2505.23135, DafnyBench, VCoT-Bench) but every one is a STATIC curated set; none mints. (3) THE DIFFICULTY LABEL IS A THEOREM. Unimodular conjugation preserves tensor rank, so on every minted instance rank 7 stays achievable and rank 6 stays impossible BY THEOREM, transported not re-measured. A 2026 survey line states the complementary gap outright: dynamic benchmarks such as DyVal 'provide no mathematical guarantees that each generated problem instance is well-posed, resulting in ambiguous correctness labels and evaluation pipelines that must rely on heuristic matching.' That sentence is the pitch. The static/dynamic axis is not.
targets.measured: THE PROTOTYPE IS A WALL, NOT A RULER, AND THIS IS ON OUR OWN PAGE. reports/matmul-eval.html §disguise rung, first campaign: on fixed d7, opus-5 certified. On minted instance c1 (denser after conjugation, entries to |8|) opus-5 and sonnet-5 returned EMPTY TEXT on every attempt, exhausting the output budget; haiku attempted every time and was exactly rejected every time. Final table is all zeros. A benchmark on which every model scores 0 measures nothing and ranks nobody — it cannot even order the frontier, which is the one thing a leaderboard must do.
targets.next: THE FIRST JOB IS NOT TO BUILD, IT IS TO FIND A RUNG WITH A NON-ZERO, NON-SATURATED SCORE. Difficulty must become a dial with the theorem riding along: conjugation entries bounded by a seed-controlled parameter, so the family runs continuously from raw Strassen (trivially recalled, must score ~1) up to c1 (currently 0). Sweep it, publish the curve, and the deliverable becomes the honest thing — a DIFFICULTY DIAL whose hardness label is proved — rather than a leaderboard of zeros. Until that curve exists there is no benchmark to publish. Streaming for deeper output budgets is named on the page as the other blocker and is probably necessary but not sufficient: haiku answered and was refuted, so emptiness is not purely a budget artifact.
targets.note: Also worth carrying: 'recall provably scores zero' is a stronger claim than any incumbent makes and is the red control that should lead the write-up — RAW Strassen must FAIL on a conjugated instance. That is a falsifier, and it is the part of this that is genuinely ours.

targets.name: Industrialize refutation — sweep every checkable conjecture that nobody has checked
targets.verdict: OPEN but narrowed — the PROVING lane just closed, the REFUTING lane did not
targets.occupied: The obvious framing was taken three weeks ago. OEIS OPEN (arXiv:2608.11941, Tom Adamczewski, 12 Aug 2026): 492 open OEIS conjectures formalized in Lean as a benchmark, secured against model cheating, models resolved 147 of them — 30% on the full set, 44% on Lite; giving models 476,000 arXiv papers did not help. Older prior art in the same lane: Sloane's 'Prove or Disprove: 100 Conjectures from the OEIS' (math/0409509) and Mathar's automated proofs of conjectured OEIS recurrences (arXiv:1707.04654). erdosproblems.com plus teorth/erdosproblems is already the live status database for the Erdos corpus, actively maintained with AI assistance.
targets.gap: OEIS Open is about turning conjectures INTO THEOREMS in Lean. It does not refute, and it does not check anything numerically past the listed terms — the complement of what this engine does. Our one demonstrated hit, erdos852, was exactly that: data sitting in the OEIS since 2002, a conjecture never checked against it, a record found and extended. Certified numerical REFUTATION past the published range is the lane, and 'a REFUTED here is proved' is the thing no sampling sweep can say.
targets.measured: NOTHING. The yield is n = 1. One hit is an anecdote, not a rate.
targets.next: MEASURE THE YIELD BEFORE INDUSTRIALISING ANYTHING. Sample N OEIS comments of the 'it appears that' / 'conjecture' form that are cheaply checkable, run the existing engine, and count: refuted, held, not-checkable-for-lack-of-data. That number decides whether this is a graveyard or an empty field, and it costs one run. If the rate is near zero the idea dies cheaply; if it is a few percent the live conjecture graveyard is real and the 'how long it stood before anyone looked' column is genuinely unbuilt anywhere.
targets.note: tools/sweep-claims.js already runs a narrow version of this watch. The honest framing is never 'progress on X' — it is 'checked where nothing was checked'.

targets.name: A registry where any published number can be re-derived — a DOI for numbers
targets.verdict: DEAD as a standard — the technical layer exists and has failed on adoption, twice
targets.killedBy: The mechanism is not the missing piece and has not been for a decade. NANOPUBLICATIONS plus TRUSTY URIs are precisely this design, in production: a claim published as a small machine-readable object with assertion + provenance + publication-info, addressed by a URI that CONTAINS a hash of its own content, so any link carries the means to verify what it points at (arXiv:1401.5775; PeerJ CS 78). Alongside them: ACM artifact-evaluation badging, ReScience, Whole Tale, Zenodo DOIs. Everything the proposal describes as new is deployed and specified. What has never happened is uptake, and uptake is not an engineering problem we can out-build.
targets.why: It also fails this repository's own killer-app test (CLAUDE.md, app doctrine): a contested rule with no compelled buyer is a demo, not a market. Nobody is legally required to re-derive a number in a paper, so there is no one who must buy the answer. Compare SkyAudit, where the buyer is compelled by a rule.
targets.note: The RESIDUE IS WORTH KEEPING and is already what this machine does: re-derivation as a SERVICE aimed at one number that someone actually disputes, published as an audit page — rm-audit, zeta3-audit, matmul-additions are that product and it works. Do those; do not attempt to found a standard.

targets.name: An atlas of what is actually known — certified intervals on the numbers civilization steers by
targets.verdict: DEAD as stated — the premise is false about every field it names
targets.killedBy: The claim that 'nobody has drawn the map' is wrong in each named domain, and the map is the field's flagship product. CODATA publishes the fundamental physical constants with standard uncertainties on a fixed revision cycle — that IS the atlas for physics, and it is more carefully made than anything we would produce. IPCC publishes likely ranges for climate sensitivity. Cochrane publishes confidence intervals for drug effect sizes as the entire point of a systematic review. Economic elasticities come with standard errors. The point estimate everyone quotes already has a published width beside it.
targets.why: The one genuine difference — a CERTIFIED enclosure versus a statistical confidence interval — is not a difference our instruments can supply here. Our certifiers decide exact arithmetic questions; the width on a climate sensitivity or a drug effect is irreducibly statistical and no amount of exact rational arithmetic converts an empirical estimate into an enclosure. Attempting it would mean re-deriving primary data field by field, at civilizational scale, to produce something weaker than what is already published. Fails the killer-app test as well: no compelled buyer for the atlas as a whole.
targets.note: The residue is the app doctrine already in CLAUDE.md, arrived at from the other direction: pick ONE domain where a published rule compels somebody to produce a defensible number, pin the data, and certify against the rule. That is the DECIDABLE-CLAIMS OBSERVATORY template and it is idea 4 done correctly, one city at a time.

targets.name: A public board of provably inconsistent aircraft tracks, from ADS-B
targets.verdict: OPEN — the data is already here; the scope is the constraint, not the feed
targets.premiseFalse: CORRECTED 2026-08-31, and the correction runs the other way. THE FIRST HALF WAS WRONG: SkyAudit DOES ingest ADS-B, daily. apps/skyaudit/audit/ingest-day.js downloads an adsb.lol day, sha256-pins it, extracts, certifies, re-flies and compares, and eight pinned days sit on disk (2026-08-23..30) with full traces in nyc.full.jsonl. The earlier row read only SOURCES-PINS.json — which pins the regulatory and academic PDFs — and concluded there was no traffic feed. There is. 'Zero new data' HOLDS for the track board. THE SECOND HALF STANDS AND IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: the traces carry position, barometric altitude, ground speed and track, all self-reported, with no pseudoranges — so 'does any position/clock solution exist consistent with all observables' is still NOT decidable from this feed. Kinematic infeasibility is, and that is still the honest scope.
targets.occupied: The public-map idea is taken twice over, commercially and academically. SkAI Data Services runs a LIVE GPS spoofing and jamming tracker (spoofing.skai-data-services.com) on OpenSky ADS-B, flagging spoofed aircraft in real time. GPSJAM.org aggregates ADS-B NIC/NACp into daily hex grids. OPSGROUP publishes a pilot-facing spoofing map. Stanford SCPNT published 'Observations of GNSS Spoofing in Russia in 2023-2024' (ION ITM 2025). The detection literature is deep and mostly ML: LSTM encoder-decoder anomaly detection (arXiv:1711.10192), VizADS-B (arXiv:1906.07921), RDPA dual-domain deep learning (2026), TDOA multilateration counter-spoofing. Never pitch 'a map of spoofing' — that exists.
targets.gap: EVERY INCUMBENT IS A DETECTOR; NONE IS A DECIDER. GPSJAM aggregates a SELF-REPORTED quality indicator — it measures what the aircraft says about its own accuracy. SkAI flags 'potentially spoofed'. The ML work emits scores and needs a threshold. Not one of them can say a thing is IMPOSSIBLE. Our grammar can: no state trajectory exists consistent with all reports and their bounds, therefore a report is false, with the witness attached. That verdict is permanent, citable, and cannot be argued with — the same property that makes a REFUTED here worth more than a sampling check.
targets.scopeWarning: BE HONEST ABOUT WHAT IS PROVABLE FROM A BARE ADS-B FEED. Self-reported position plus NIC/NACp does NOT carry raw pseudoranges, so 'does any position/clock solution exist consistent with all observables' is NOT decidable from it — that question needs receiver-level or multi-station TDOA data we do not have. What IS decidable and provable from the feed alone is KINEMATIC infeasibility: consecutive reports requiring an acceleration, speed or climb rate outside any envelope the airframe admits; two positions and a timestamp that no aircraft can join. Scope the board to that and every row is a proof. Everything else is NEEDS DATA, naming the receiver or the second station that would settle it — which is the sharpest product edge we have and no incumbent offers it.
targets.note: Set-membership GNSS integrity, the mathematical core of the proposal's #1 and #3, is fifteen years old: robust set-inversion via interval analysis (SIVIA) computing guaranteed 3-D location zones in real time, with infeasibility already read as fault (Drevelle and Bonnifait, GPS Solutions, height-aided high-integrity positioning). Our differentiator is exact rational arithmetic — an empty set that is PROVED rather than numerically conditioned — plus the three-valued grammar. It is not the technique.

targets.name: The glide ring as a band: an inner ring you provably reach and an outer you provably cannot
targets.verdict: OPEN — the strongest artifact on the aviation list, and the instrument already exists here
targets.occupied: The single-line version ships from everyone: Garmin Glide Range Ring, ForeFlight Glide Advisor, LXNAV glide range area, all drawing one boundary from terrain, GPS, winds aloft and a nominal best-glide ratio. Academic work covers gliding reachable regions with obstacles and wind (arXiv:2407.18056, arXiv:2304.06499) and airspace-aware contingency landing (arXiv:2602.07074). Patents exist on engine-out range display (US 11511883).
targets.gap: NOBODY SHIPS THE BAND, and the literature computes optimal glides rather than guaranteed envelopes. Every shipped ring is a point estimate drawn as a promise, and the inputs it rests on are all uncertain: wind aloft is a forecast, weight is estimated, glide ratio is nominal and degrades with a windmilling prop, terrain has a stated vertical accuracy. The honest object is two boundaries with a hatched annulus between them, and the annulus is exactly where a pilot is currently given false confidence at the worst possible moment. That picture has never been drawn.
targets.fit: THE INSTRUMENT IS ALREADY BUILT AND SHIPPED HERE, in different clothing. reports/evtol-energy.html certifies a provable energy-reserve envelope from interval-valued inputs — usable capacity [130,145] kWh, efficiency [0.88,0.94], reserve power [90,110] kW — against a hard regulatory rule (the FAA powered-lift SFAR 20-minute VFR / 30-minute IFR reserve). A glide band is the same certified-envelope logic with a different state equation, and it inherits the same compelled-buyer shape.
targets.product: The doctrine's disclosure lever applies directly and is what makes it a product rather than a picture: publish the threshold that FLIPS each airport's verdict — 'at 12 kt more headwind this field leaves the inner ring'. Airports coloured by which zone they fall in; the tri-state in plain words, never colour alone (Garmin grammar); predicted wind and decided reachability never sharing a typography (the prediction-as-proposer rule).
targets.cost: Needs a terrain DEM — the two pmtiles in the repo are basemap, not elevation. SRTM or Copernicus DEM is free, small, and pinnable, so this is the cheapest new-data ask on the list.
targets.hazard: HIGHEST hazard-word exposure of anything here. 'Certified' in aviation means airworthiness. tools/build-report-skyaudit.js and build-report-evtol-energy.js already carry the discipline in a header comment — certified always means a mathematically certified enclosure, no airworthiness meaning, said on the page where a reader could trip. Any glide artifact must carry it louder, plus an explicit not-for-navigation label, because this one depicts an emergency procedure.

targets.name: Exactly certified Gaussian overbounding for ARAIM protection levels
targets.verdict: OPEN technically, WRONG FIRST MOVE commercially — cite it, do not build it
targets.finding: Correctly ranked last by the proposal itself. The technical fit is the best on the list: overbounding — proving a nominal error distribution bounds the real one — is the load-bearing assumption of the whole integrity architecture and is done today with margins and floating point. An exact rational proof of 'this bounds that' is a genuine contribution, and DO-178C/DO-254 evidence is the most expensive line in avionics development, so the buyer is compelled and rich.
targets.why: But it is unreachable as a first artifact: we have no access to a certification evidence chain, no receiver data, and no design-assurance standing, and the sales cycle is measured in years. It is also adjacent to fifteen years of set-membership GNSS integrity work, so the novelty is the arithmetic, not the idea.
targets.note: USE IT AS THE CREDENTIAL PARAGRAPH, not the deliverable. One paragraph in an outreach page — 'the same arithmetic that decides this glide band is what an exactly certified overbound would need' — tells an avionics engineer we understand where their real cost sits, without promising anything we cannot ship.

targets.name: Assured PNT and certifying autonomy that cannot be exhaustively tested
targets.verdict: OPEN as a direction — right diagnosis, and the scale gap is real and should be said out loud
targets.finding: Two stated Western defence priorities, and both are our grammar rather than our scale. Assured PNT is explicitly about BOUNDED, trustworthy position rather than merely accurate position — which is the protection-level object, and the same instrument as the ADS-B and overbound rows. Certifying autonomy is the harder and more interesting one: the field is trying to do it with statistics over test campaigns, and 'we ran 10,000 sorties' is a fundamentally different claim from 'this behaviour is proved safe over the whole input envelope, or provably unsafe, or undecided — and here is exactly the measurement that would decide it'. The three-valued envelope verdict is structurally, not incrementally, different.
targets.bridge: The honest bridge already exists and is aerospace-shaped: the eVTOL reserve certificate proves a property over an envelope of uncertain inputs against a published rule, and REFUSES where the instance does not close. That is a miniature of the autonomy argument, in a domain with a real regulator, and it is shippable now. Lead with it; let the autonomy claim be the direction it points at, never a capability asserted.
targets.note: sin-mfg's EMBRAERX_SCOPING.md holds the outreach rule this front should run under, and it is the right one: ARTIFACT BEFORE ASK — no contact is spent until the door-opener report exists, and every fact used in outreach is re-verified at source at send time. That probe also has verified UAM sources and a capability-to-need map worth reading before writing any defence or airspace page.

targets.name: The certified glide band — BUILT and evolved, reports/glide-band.html
targets.verdict: BUILT 2026-08-31 — shipped, gated, and honest about what it is not
targets.finding: The headline is not the one the scout expected, and it is better. The comparison against the incumbent method is NOT 'their ring is too big'. It is that WHILE THE PANEL'S ASSUMED INPUTS SIT INSIDE THE HONEST ENVELOPE, ITS LINE ALWAYS FALLS BETWEEN THE TWO CERTIFIED BOUNDARIES — so no airfield inside that line can ever be proved unreachable. The single line cannot be caught being wrong, and it is never shown to be right either: 57% of what it claims is undecided by the evidence it was drawn from. An instrument that cannot fail a test is not passing one. That is a structural claim, it is gated at build (the build refuses if a mode-0 refutation ever appears), and it is sharper than any percentage.
targets.measured: Pinned adsb.lol flight N412JS, a PC-12 single-engine turboprop at FL240, 2026-08-26, via apps/skyaudit’s day pin. 320 airfields (OurAirports, public domain, sha256-pinned), 480 states = 16 cruise positions x 5 illustrative aircraft packs x 3 winds x 2 forecast modes. THE THREE NUMBERS: with the panel configured inside the envelope, 54% of the site-states inside its line are unproved and 0 are refutable (structural, gated). With the propeller NOT feathered — same aircraft, same flight, one action short, and the glass has no way to know — 29% of what the same line shows becomes PROVABLY unreachable, Philadelphia International among them. With the winds-aloft forecast 180 degrees out, 27%.
targets.note: TWO THINGS THAT NEARLY WENT WRONG AND ARE WORTH REMEMBERING. (1) The first battery had a red control that fired VACUOUSLY — an assert.ok(false) at the end of the loop guaranteed it regardless of whether the loop tested anything. That is sin-mfg's vacuous-green failure reproduced from scratch; it is now a real mutant that grades against the nominal ring and reports the disagreement count. (2) The first attempt to produce refutations was going to raise a 'book glide ratio' constant until crosses appeared. That is tuning a number until the story works. The honest refutation case is a REVERSED WINDS-ALOFT FORECAST — a documented failure of the input the ring leans on hardest — and it needed no tuning at all. EVOLVED 2026-08-31 (operator: “use illustrative scenarios to fill the missing parameters”). Two additions carried the weight. (1) FIVE ILLUSTRATIVE PACKS instead of one anonymous envelope — trainer, high-performance single, turboprop feathered, turboprop NOT feathered, glider — each a stated class with a stated envelope AND the ratio the panel would be configured with. The fourth is the whole point: identical aircraft and flight, and the failure is not a bad number but an event the instrument cannot observe. That is a far better second scenario than the reversed forecast because nobody had to choose a value for it. (2) THE TURN (H5): height lost turning onto each field at standard rate from the aircraft’s ACTUAL ADS-B ground track, charged to BOTH instruments so the comparison stays about method. It makes the band visibly asymmetric about the flight path rather than a ring centred on the aeroplane, and it uses real pinned data rather than an assumption.
targets.next: Terrain is H1 and is the next build: the same arithmetic over a pinned DEM turns green fields amber and never the reverse, so it only ever costs claims. After that the honest asks are real performance data (which would narrow H4 and shrink the annulus, which is the point) and the fact that none of this is DO-178C evidence.
